A novel AI method for vertebral bone detection in CT scans incorporates rectification techniques to improve robustness and ease, and incorporates constraints based on vertebral anatomy to ensure precise localization of thoracic and lumbar vertebrae. By fixing the spine's longitudinal axis and making bilateral symmetry assumptions in relation to vertebral morphology, the method minimizes the impact of image distortion and non-standard patient positions. Once the vertebral bodies are identified, the system conducts a series of optimizations to determine their precise alignment, and in conjunction, the system is designed to automatically recognize each vertebral level. A multi-faceted approach to error correction and reliability assessment are employed to counterbalance potential vertebral counting discrepancies. We trained and tested our fully automated system using CT scans of both standard and irregular spinal configurations, and verified its effectiveness in localizing and identifying all vertebral levels with high accuracy. Quantitative evaluation revealed the following results: thresholding based on distance maps yielded 98.6% precise vertebral localization, and convolutional neural network based vertebral recognition achieved an accuracy rate of 93.4%. Moreover, the system automatically determined the correct number of vertebras in the lumbar region with 100% accuracy for 65-scans, and a lumbar miscount occurrence rate of no more than one scan in 99.6% of 75-scans. We trained and tested our systems without any parameter adjustments across different subject groups, and achieved these results despite the presence of various spinal anomalies and imaging distortions. Therefore, the proposed automation approach is versatile and suitable for use in a wide variety of subjects, and can withstand variations in vertebral morphology and imaging conditions. Electron scattering off a potential barrier in a confined space can be affected by quantum vacuum effects if the barrier is placed within a cavity with low photon occupancy. We have investigated how these vacuum effects impact the process of electron transmission when a square potential barrier is situated within a cavity in two different scenarios. These studies were conducted in a range of ripples generated by the photon vacuum effect in a cavity, with the ripples' amplitudes increasing as the parameter $\sqrt{n}\lambda_d$ (where $\lambda_d$ represents the dipole matrix element) varies from weak to ultrastrong coupling. In the first scenario, in which the ripples' amplitudes increase slowly, the vortex structure of the vacuum effect has a substantial impact on resonant electron transmission, causing sharp increases in transmission probabilities at resonant points. In the second scenario, in which the ripples' amplitudes increase rapidly, the vortex structure of the vacuum effect becomes less significant and the transmission probability at resonant points exhibits strong increases and decreases in an oscillatory pattern. These oscillatory patterns are in agreement with the behavior of Riemann surface excursions. These findings illustrate the potential for electron scattering to be dynamically stabilized by vacuum effects against energy losses within the ultrastrong light-material coupling regime. These discoveries may contribute to advancements in various quantum technologies. They also illustrate the significance of vacuum effects in electron scattering processes in quantum mechanics. Furthermore, the study of these quantum vacuum effects in quantum parabolic potentials in a cavity, with the potential barriers situated at the centers and edges of the potential well, has yielded similar oscillatory transmission patterns in off-resonant transmission events in both scenarios. In the first case, the oscillations in transmission probabilities around the center of the well are less pronounced than those at the well's edges, while in the second case, the oscillations in transmission probabilities around both the center and the well's edges exhibit similar amplitudes and periodicities. In general, the oscillatory amplitudes in both scenarios have exhibited an inverse relationship with the dipole matrix element of the potential well and a direct relationship with the photon vacuum effect's characteristic scale $n^{-1/2}$. These studies have been performed in the ultrastrong light-material coupling regime in a quantum optics context, with the electron scattering processes in a one-dimensional quantum system in a cavity. They have been supported by the exact numerical solutions of the one-dimensional time-dependent Schrodinger equation in a quantum optics context. This research explores the capabilities of deep reinforcement learning for the control of elastic actuators in quadruped robotics, showing that successful movement can be achieved in scenarios previously thought only feasible with rigid actuators, significantly reducing power consumption and improving robustness. By leveraging the elastic actuator's properties to pass forces to the ground, a custom interaction model was developed that enhances training efficiency and optimizes the integration of actuator stiffness and movement parameters. Experimental results obtained with a physical prototype based on the Sprat-lab's quadruped robot demonstrate the effectiveness of the elastic actuator-based control system. Related works and practical considerations are thoroughly discussed in the accompanying thesis. A crucial concept in fashion search is trait manipulation. Research has been conducted to achieve trait transfer in images, which holds significant potential for improving fashion search outcomes. Prior approaches, however, have primarily focused on image-level manipulation and relied on the underlying assumption that manipulating images would lead to trait changes. Nonetheless, this assumption may not always hold true, especially in the fashion context. Moreover, defining and quantifying traits poses a significant challenge. To address these issues, we propose a novel semi-supervised method for feature-level trait manipulation. Our method performs trait embedding during the pre-training phase to establish a mapping between traits and compact vectors, which are then combined with style encodings through a semi-supervised approach. This method enables fine-grained trait manipulation at the feature level while also reducing the need for extensive annotation. Our results demonstrate the efficacy of this method in generating plausible images with a focus on visual consistency. The relationship between primal and dual problems is a central concept in optimization that has far-reaching implications in various areas of applied mathematics, not only in finding optimal solutions but also in regularizing ill-posed problems. In this paper, we establish a connection between primal and dual gradient descent methods in Banach space settings, investigate their cooling effects, and demonstrate the conditions under which these methods can produce images with minimal error rates. Our analysis reveals that the primal-dual relationship has an intricate influence on the convergence rates of these methods, often resulting in equivalent convergence rates under certain constraints for primal and dual models. By exploring the cooling strategy, we prove that even if the primal model lacks a fast convergence rate, the dual descent method can still yield spurious artifact-free results after a sufficient time, outperforming primal methods in this aspect. Furthermore, our findings highlight the practical implications of using dual descent as a post-processing technique that can improve solutions obtained through primal descent, thereby alleviating the overfitting issue and achieving high-quality image recovery in complex Banach space models. Lastly, through challenging experiments and theoretical calculations, we validate the efficacy of dual descent as the optimal regularized learning paradigm for neural networks trained on functional data. Our research substantiates that dual descent offers superior performance and achieves better results than primal descent, thereby emerging as the preferred method for regularized learning in Banach space settings. Implementation details and source code for our experiments are publicly accessible at the repository: https://github.com/damooster/PrimalDualGD. The analytical results were initially reported in our paper: dual gradient descent for regularized learning in Banach space settings, published at arXiv:2109.09479. A novel, deep learning-based approach has been developed for light field depth estimation using occlusion awareness. Called the Occlusion-Aware Expense Creator (OACE), it aims to model occlusion in the optimization process and reduce unnecessary computation during the optimization of each pixel's depth. OACE significantly improves the precision of light field depth estimation by introducing a novel layer that calculates occlusion likelihood and adjusts the optimization process with constraint weights. Experimental results on the standard "Buddha" dataset, as well as newly collected datasets "OcclusionLF" and "TableOcclusionLF", demonstrate that OACE successfully achieves high accurate depth estimates with a low number of linear combinations, and that the introduced occlusion-awareness method enhances overall estimation performance. Quantitative analysis suggests that OACE's success can be attributed to the incorporation of occlusion-specific factors during optimization. OACE's superior performance is further established by comprehensive benchmarking of state-of-the-art light field depth estimation methods using both conventional and occlusion-aware approaches. The Fokas-Lenells equation, an extension of the well-known ALD equation, was first introduced in the late 1990s. In response, certain notable results were achieved, including the Fokas-Lenells bilinear approach, which yields the integrals of the Fokas-Lenells equation as well as new solutions for the ALD equation. Subsequently, this method was applied to a equation that combines the features of the nonlinear Schrödinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations. A short time later, another system was discovered that shares properties with the Fokas-Lenells equation; known as the Fokas-Ablowitz-Lenells system, it was defined by taking the square root of the equation's Lax operator. Progress on this new system led to the discovery of multiple interesting solutions, although an explicit solution for the time-like equation remained elusive until a study in 2019. In 2020, a series of papers successfully applied the Fokas-Lenells bilinear method to the time-like equation, first the SL(2, R) affine Gelfand-Dikii system and then the Bessel equation. A year later, this same approach was applied to a equation that shares properties with the ALD equation but includes an additional nonlinear term. Given the relatively limited amount of literature on this equation, it will be referred to as the extended ALD (eALD) equation. Through the bilinear method, this study demonstrates the existence of multiple solutions to the extended ALD equation as well as the integrals of its Lax equations. Notably, one of the first solutions obtained was explicitly shown to be a Wronskian solution; in addition, a new type of soliton solution was also found. Furthermore, the approach used in this study can be adapted for use in Lax equations where the Fokas-Lenells equation and extended ALD equation differ by more than a sign. A related work on the extended GLD equation, first the square root then the Lax operator, was also carried out. During this time, the GLD and GLD systems were found to be two distinct systems whose equations are not even locally commutative under certain conditions. In a final work on the extended GLD equation, the concept of the new Fokas-Lenells formula was discovered; in doing so, the study yields the first explicit solution obtained through the bilinear method for the time-like equation. A novel effective action for gravity, incorporating a higher-derivative term, is developed within the context of double field gravity. This theory's action is characterized by a uniquely defined coefficient, unrestricted by specific backgrounds or frames. When considering backgrounds with vanishing dilaton and with Christoffel connection, the resulting equation of motion takes the form of a Lanczos tensor equation. This particular equation is known to be invulnerable to frame transformations and provides a means of defining a conformal static manifold. The article also provides an example of a conformally static 2S-KG wave-space, highlighting its link to LPF gravity, and finally, it identifies the conditions under which the Lanczos equation results in the Einstein equation with a traceless Ricci tensor. Nonetheless, it's evident that Einstein's equation, even with this condition, still admits non-Riemannian structures. Moreover, the article delves into the possibility of defining a more generalized energy-momentum tensor $(\Theta_{AB}, \bar{\Theta}_{AB})$, however, it's found to be symmetric only under the condition specified in the Lanczos equation. This energy-momentum tensor is linked to a gravitationally-induced charge, separable from the center-of-mass charge, and defined within the 2S-KG wave-space as the gradient of its surface charge density. The article's central aim is to demonstrate that the Lanczos equation, though non-Riemannian and non-conservative, still enables the definition of a positive, bounded below, and physically interpretable energy-momentum tensor, even in scenarios characterized by non-Riemannian structures. However, it's crucial to note that the article's conclusions hold true for general gravitational systems, effective actions involving higher derivatives, and even in contexts involving deformations of the DFT background. Thus, the article's findings are distinguished by their broad applicability to numerous gravitational theories. The article is thus aimed at a broader audience, including those working with a variety of gravitational systems. To maximize profits, ISPs can increase data-hungry customers' access to by installing more APs or extending existing ones, however, deciding the best course of action involves numerous variables to consider. We suggest employing IEEE 802.11k/v standards to measure the channel quality and use machine learning algorithms to process this data and determine whether to set up new APs or add to existing ones by analyzing their individual performance. We test our method on 34 houses and compare it to other learning and modeling techniques, revealing that it outperforms them by nearly 25% in predicting optimal AP configurations, resulting in a significantly shorter simulation time of around 81%. Moreover, we attribute the success of our approach to the effectiveness of using channel load metrics in conjunction with channel width information. This work aims to aid ISPs in choosing between deploying new APs or expanding existing ones and can be applied by ISPs to optimize their WiFi network configurations.
